unsupported_claims: LINE's experiments used K = 5 negative samples per edge (as I recall from the paper's parameter settings)

Per step, the work grows linearly in K (and in the embedding dimension d), since each of the K negative edges adds one more O(d) update - this is consistent with the stated O(d(K+1)) but is an inference beyond the explicit text
rationale: The evidence gives no chosen numerical value for K, so the claim that LINE used K = 5 is an invented specific that the papers do not support, even though it is hedged as recollection. The statements that the paper does not describe effects of changing K beyond O(d(K+1)) and that the per-step cost is linear in K are supported by the stated complexity formula.
